source_text:
6 Λεγέσθω περὶ Ἀντωνίου καὶ ταῦτα τῆς Ἰερεμίου προφητείας τὰ ῥήματα·
«Πρὸ τοῦ με πλάσαι σε ἐν κοιλίᾳ, ἐπίσταμαί σε καὶ πρὸ τοῦ <σε> ἐξελθεῖν ἐκ μήτρας
ἡγίακά σε»· τὴν γὰρ ἁγιωσύνην ὡς σύντροφον ἐπετήδευε. Κλῆρον ἐκ μήτρας τὴν
ἁγίαν ἐκέκτητο ταπείνωσιν καὶ φιλοσοφίας ἀρχὴν τὴν σωφροσύνην τὴν διὰ Χριστοῦ
ἔθετο. ∆εῦρο καὶ τοῦτον ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Ἰὼβ ἱστορίας ἐνδύσωμεν τῇ κεφαλῇ τοῦ δικαίου
τὸν στέφανον· «Ἄνθρωπος γὰρ ἦν ἐν χώρᾳ τῇ» κατ' Αἴγυπτον, ὄνομα Ἀντώνιος,
«ἄνθρωπος ἄμεμπτος, ἀληθινός, θεοσεβής, δίκαιος, ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ παντὸς πονηροῦ
πράγματος» καὶ «ἦν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος εὐγενὴς τῶν ἀφ' ἡλίου ἀνατολῶν.» Ἡλίου
ποίου; –Τοῦ τῆς δικαιοσύνης· ἐκείνου γὰρ ἀνατολαὶ ὑπῆρχον οἱ ἀπόστολοι, ὧν τὴν
συγγένειαν Ἀντώνιος εἶχε· ἡ περιβολὴ τῆς εὐγενείας τοῦ πνεύματος καλείσθω.
7 Καὶ Σολομών τι περὶ τοῦ δικαίου τούτου καὶ αὐτὸς παροι-μιάσασθαι
δύναται· «Μέγα ἄνθρωπος καὶ τίμιον ἀνὴρ ἐλεήμων, ἄνδρα δὲ πιστὸν ἔργον εὑρεῖν.»
Εὕραμεν τοίνυν, εὕραμεν ἡμεῖς τὸν τῷ σοφῷ ζητούμενον, ἀλλ' ὁ μὲν ἔλεγεν ἄνδρα
πιστὸν εὑρεῖν, Παῦλος δὲ οὐχ οὕτως. Ἀλλὰ τί φησιν; – «Οἳ διὰ πίστεως
κατηγωνίσαντο βασιλείας», Ἀντώνιον καὶ τοὺς ἐκείνου ζηλωτὰς αἰνιττόμενος·
οὗτος γὰρ τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου, δόξαν, τιμήν τε καὶ πλοῦτον ὑπερφρονῶν
κατεπάλαισεν, «ἐπέτυχεν ἐπαγγελιῶν» τοῦ μέλλοντος, «ἔφραξε στόματα λεόντων»
τῶν ἡδο νῶν, «ἔφυγε τὰ στόματα μαχαίρας» τὴν ἔξωθεν σοφίαν, «ἐνεδυναμώθη ἀπὸ
ἀσθενείας» τῆς ἀκρατείας, «ἐγενήθη ἰσχυρὸς ἐν πολέμῳ» τῷ πρὸς τὸν διάβολον,
«παρεμβολὰς ἔκλινεν ἀλλοτρίων» τῶν δαιμόνων. «Ἔλαβον γυναῖκες ἐξ
ἀναστάσεως τοὺς νεκροὺς αὐτῶν» ὅσαι μητέρες ἁμαρτωλοὺς παῖδας τῷ δικαίῳ
προσήνεγκαν.
thought_title: Antony sanctified from the womb and crowned by Job and Paul
orientation: Hesychius continues praising Antony by applying words of Jeremiah, Job, Solomon, and Paul to him.
pass_a_gloss: Let these words too of the prophecy of Jeremiah be said concerning Antony: 'Before me to form you in belly, I know you, and before you to come out from womb I sanctified you'; for he practiced holiness as a companion. As an inheritance from the womb he possessed holy humility, and he laid down as beginning of the ascetic life the self-restraint that is through Christ. Come, let us also from the story of Job put this crown on the head of the righteous man: 'For there was a man in the land' in Egypt, by name Antony, 'a blameless man, true, God-fearing, righteous, holding himself away from every wicked deed' and 'that man was noble among those from sunrises of the sun.' Of what sun? Of the sun of righteousness; for his sunrises were the apostles, whose kinship Antony had; let the covering be called the nobility of the spirit. And Solomon himself is also able to speak as a proverb something concerning this righteous man: 'Man is a great thing and precious is a merciful man, but to find a faithful man is a hard thing.' We have found then, we have found the one sought by the wise man, but he said to find a faithful man, but Paul not thus. But what does he say? 'Who through faith fought down kingdoms,' hinting at Antony and his zealots; for he, despising the kingdoms of the world, glory and honor and wealth, wrestled them down, 'he obtained promises' of the future, 'he stopped mouths of lions' of pleasures, 'he fled the mouths of sword' of the wisdom from outside, 'he was made strong from weakness' of lack of self-control, 'he became strong in war' against the devil, 'he turned aside camps of strangers' of the demons. 'Women received from resurrection their dead,' as many mothers as brought sinful children to the righteous man.

pass_b_english: Let these words from Jeremiah's prophecy be spoken of Antony as well: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you came forth from the womb I sanctified you" (Jeremiah 1:5). For he practiced holiness as a companion brought up alongside him. From the womb he possessed holy humility as his inheritance, and through Christ he made temperance the beginning of his ascetic life.

Come, let us also crown this righteous man from the story of Job, and set this crown upon his head. There was a man in the land of Egypt whose name was Antony, "a blameless, true, God-fearing and righteous man, who held himself back from every evil deed" (Job 1:1). And "that man was noble among those from the risings of the sun" (Job 1:3). Which sun? The Sun of Righteousness. For his sunrises were the apostles, whose kinship Antony shared. Let the mantle of nobility be called that of the Spirit.

Solomon too can speak a proverb about this righteous man: "A man is great, and a merciful man is precious, but to find a faithful man is a hard thing" (Proverbs 20:6). We have found, yes we have found, the one the wise man was seeking. He spoke of finding a faithful man, but Paul does not speak that way. What does Paul say? "Who through faith fought down kingdoms" (Hebrews 11:33-35), hinting at Antony and those who imitate his zeal. For Antony despised the kingdoms of the world, glory and honor and wealth, and wrestled them to the ground. He "obtained promises" of the age to come, "shut the mouths of lions," that is the pleasures, and "escaped the mouths of the sword," that is the wisdom from outside. He "was made strong out of weakness," that is out of lack of self-control, "became mighty in war," that is the war against the devil, and "routed the armies of foreigners," that is the demons. And "women received back their dead by resurrection," that is all the mothers who brought their sinful children to the righteous man.
notes: source has editorial <σε> in Jeremiah quote; line-break παροι-μιάσασθαι and spaced ἡδο νῶν read as παροιμιάσασθαι and ἡδονῶν; κατ᾽ Αἴγυπτον is author insertion into Job quote

problems.why: In modern English 'incontinence' primarily means loss of bladder or bowel control; ἀκρατεία here means lack of self-control or intemperance.
problems.fix: that is out of lack of self-control
problems.ruling: ἀκρατείας is moral intemperance; modern 'incontinence' suggests bodily loss, misleading ascetic context.

edits.new: that is out of lack of self-control

fixed: Fixed 'that is out of incontinence': source τῆς ἀκρατείας means lack of self-control, not bladder/bowel incontinence.

problems.quote: Let his clothing be called the nobility of the Spirit.
problems.source_quote: ἡ περιβολὴ τῆς εὐγενείας τοῦ πνεύματος καλείσθω.
problems.why: Τῆς εὐγενείας is genitive modifying ἡ περιβολή ("mantle of nobility"), not a predicate nominative; τοῦ πνεύματος is the predicate ("of the Spirit"), and "his" is not in the Greek.
problems.fix: Let the mantle of nobility be called that of the Spirit.
problems.ruling: περιβολὴ τῆς εὐγενείας is mantle of nobility; English makes nobility the predicate and adds his.

edits.old: Let his clothing be called the nobility of the Spirit.
edits.new: Let the mantle of nobility be called that of the Spirit.

fixed: Fixed mistranslation of ἡ περιβολὴ τῆς εὐγενείας τοῦ πνεύματος καλείσθω: περιβολὴ τῆς εὐγενείας is the subject (mantle of nobility), τοῦ πνεύματος is the predicate, with no `his` in the Greek.
